hypothesis: Low-pass RTP-magnetic and isostatic-gravity gradient tensors will distinguish strike-extended near-2-D structures from compact 3-D bodies; retaining only ridges whose tensor eigenvector strike agrees with the ridge axis may recover whole withheld fault segments better than random ridges.
mechanism: Band-limit each scalar potential-field grid and compute its gradient tensor independently within the four official GeoDAWN acquisition blocks; derive a dimensionality index from tensor eigenvalues and strike from the quasi-2-D eigenvector; suppress compact signatures and east-west flight-line stripes; evaluate strike concordance on held-out whole fault segments.
named_non_fault_mimic: Long lithologic contacts, dikes, intrusive bodies, volcanic/vent sources, acquisition-block seams, east-west flight-line striping, tie-line/leveling residuals, and FFT edge artifacts can mimic or distort the target signature.
